title: Privacy policy
description: What personal data Mock Partner collects, why, who processes it, how long we keep it, and how to download or delete your data under UK GDPR.
intro: This policy explains what personal data we collect when you use Mock Partner, why we collect it, who helps us process it, and your rights under UK data protection law (UK GDPR). Effective date: [effective date].

blocks.text: Who we are
[legal entity name] runs Mock Partner and is the controller of your personal data. Company number: [company number]. Registered address: [registered address]. Contact: [support email].
[Founder: check whether you need to pay the ICO data protection fee and, if so, add the registration number here.]
What we collect

items: Your email address, to create your account and log you in.
Your profile: an optional country, and whether you want marketing emails (off unless you say yes).
Your plan: which plan you are on, its status and when it ends.

Your interviews: the messages you and the AI interviewer write (the transcript), a short summary of longer interviews, the numbers you give for maths questions and whether they were right, and your debrief and scores.
Your drill answers: which drills you tried, whether you got them right and how long you took.
AI usage: how much text (in tokens) each interview used and an estimate of what it cost. We use this to apply fair-use limits and control costs.
Payments: your Stripe customer reference and a reference for your subscription or payment. Stripe takes your card details on its own page. We never see or store them.

Usage events: simple records such as "started a case" or "started checkout", with the page and any campaign tags in the link you arrived from. They may be linked to your account. We don't store IP addresses in them.
Enquiries: if you contact us for a university or club, your organisation's name, your email address, the group's size and your message.

blocks.text: We don't ask for your name, school or employer, and the AI interviewer is set up not to ask for them. Please don't include them in your answers.

Our hosting and login providers receive your IP address and browser details when you use the site, as part of running and protecting it. [Founder to confirm how long Vercel and Supabase keep these logs.]

blocks.text: We never sell your data, and we never use it for advertising.

Your debrief scores are produced automatically, by an AI model and by code checks of your maths. They are practice feedback only. We don't use them to make any decision about you, and no firm sees them.

We may also share data if the law requires us to.
Cookies and browser storage

items: Cookies: we use only the cookies needed to keep you logged in. Our login system sets them, using Supabase. Because they are strictly necessary, we don't ask for consent for them.

Browser storage: your browser tab remembers your interview notes, your place in each set of drills, and how many drills you have tried without an account. This uses your browser's session storage, which is cleared when you close the tab. None of this is sent to us.

Campaign tags: if the link you arrived by had campaign tags (such as utm_source), your browser tab keeps those in the same session storage. They are sent to us when you sign in, and recorded with your sign-up if you are new. They are then kept with your usage events, which are deleted after 180 days.
Page-view counts: if we count page views, we use Vercel Web Analytics, which doesn't use cookies.
We don't use advertising pixels or third-party trackers. If that ever changes, we will ask for your consent first.

Share links

After an interview you can make a link that shows your scores as a card. The link itself holds everything on the card: your five skill scores, the case, the day of the interview, and a first name only if you type one. We don't store share links or keep a list of them.

Anyone with the link can see the card. Sites where you post it may keep their own copy of the preview picture. Because the link holds nothing that identifies your account, it keeps working even if you delete your account. To take a card down, delete the post or message where you shared it.
Your rights
Under UK GDPR you have the right to:

items: Get a copy of your data. On your account page, choose Download my data to get a file (in JSON format) of everything we hold about you.

Delete your account and data. On your account page, type your email address to confirm. This deletes your account, practice history and transcripts straight away. It also deletes your Stripe customer record, which cancels any subscription. Stripe keeps the payment records it is legally required to keep. Share links you made keep working (see Share links above).
Ask us to correct data that is wrong.
Object to how we use your data, or ask us to restrict it.
Take your data to another service. The download above is in a common, machine-readable format.
Withdraw your consent to marketing emails at any time.

blocks.text: For anything you can't do from your account page, email [support email]. We will reply within one month.
If you are unhappy with how we use your data, please tell us first. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK's data protection regulator, at ico.org.uk.
Keeping your data safe

items: Your data sits in a database that only lets you read your own records.
Secret keys stay on our servers and never reach your browser.
Card details never touch our site.

blocks.text: Age
Mock Partner is for people aged [minimum age, founder to confirm] and over. We don't knowingly collect data from anyone younger.
Changes to this policy
If we change this policy, we will update the date on this page. If a change matters, we will email account holders before it applies.
